style.summary:
style of A: A is brief and receptive, with 'Mmm' and 'Mm-hmm. OK' that keep B talking.
style of B: B is expansive and informal, hedging with 'whatever' and admitting to throwing too many things out.

A: A's receptive markers keep B talking, which lets A shape how long B's turns run.
A's 'OK' signals acceptance of B's points, which gives A the power to close each topic.
A's restrained tone leaves A free to judge B's examples without committing to them.
B: B's expansive style fills the space and sets the register of the exchange.
B's informal hedging presents B's points as options that B can shape.
B's self-aware remark about the amount of content shows B controls how much is said.

A: A's markers are passive, and B's decision to keep talking is what drives the turn length.
'OK' accepts points without closing topics, so B's continued talk shows B controls the close.
Judging examples without committing to them leaves A with little influence, since B sets which examples are on the table.
B: B's examples only shape the register because A invites them, so A's receptive stance decides the tone.
Long turns can be a sign of over-explaining, and A's brief replies show A sets the limit.
B's self-deprecation reads as a concession, which leaves A's silence with the final say.

content.summary:
content of A: A acknowledges and asks for nothing new, so the substance comes from B.
content of B: B supplies the technical examples of second-pass decoding, including backtrace and low-energy digit regions.

A: A's acknowledgements keep the examples in play without A adding any of its own.
A's agreement with each point lets the content stand as accepted.
A's pattern of confirmation determines which examples the group treats as settled.
B: B supplies all the technical examples, which determines what the conversation is about.
B's detail on backtrace and connected digits gives B control of the technical substance.
B's range of second-pass examples shapes what the group can consider.

A: A's acceptance of points is only meaningful if B keeps making them, so B sets the content.
Agreement without adding content is a passive stance that does not decide the substance.
B's examples determine the range of options, so A's confirmation only follows B's choices.
B: B's examples are invited by A's receptive pattern, so A's invitation shapes the content.
B's technical detail is only as useful as A's willingness to accept it.
Breadth of examples is not control, since A decides which of them are taken up.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: A gives minimal responses that leave the floor with B.
coordination of B: B holds the floor for long stretches and sets the flow of the exchange.

A: A's minimal responses let B occupy the floor, which gives A control over when B stops.
A's 'Mm-hmm. OK' prompts B to continue, so A chooses the pacing.
A's short turns keep the exchange in A's hands whenever A chooses to speak.
B: B holds the floor for long stretches, which gives B control of the flow.
B's long turns set the pace and the order of topics.
B's ability to continue without interruption shows B controls the exchange.

A: A's minimal responses are passive, so B's willingness to continue sets the flow.
A's prompts are weak, since B decides whether to carry on.
A's short turns are rare, so they do not give A real control of the exchange.
B: B's long turns exist because A allows them, so A sets the space for B.
Setting the pace only works while A keeps responding, so A can change the tempo.
B's uninterrupted turns depend on A's passivity, which means A can interrupt at any point.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: A's acknowledgements show attention but ask no questions and offer no examples.
engagement of B: B is energetic and offers several examples, with a self-aware remark about the amount of content.

A: A's attentive acknowledgements show that A is following B closely.
A's steady responses show A is invested enough to keep the exchange going.
A's attention gives A the role of a judging audience.
B: B offers several examples, showing deep engagement with the subject.
B's self-aware remark shows B is attentive to the discussion's flow.
B's energy makes B the driving force of the conversation.

A: Attention without questions or examples is a weak form of engagement.
Steady responses are passive, so they do not show a stake in the outcome.
Being an audience is a role that B's content defines.
B: Several examples are only engagement if A takes them up, which A has not yet done.
Self-awareness can be a way of deferring to A's sense of what is enough.
Energy depends on A's responses, so A's attention fuels B's contribution.
